Although I’ve already answered this question in the article, I thought I’d expound further. Consider this: If the Qur’an was meant to convey a scientific message then why didn’t earlier scholars develop scientific theories on the basis of reading the Qur’an? Why did the mufassirrun never come up with quantum physics, the big bang theory, plate tectonics, and a host of other contemporary scientific discoveries? The idea that there is “science” in the Qur’an, yet Muhammad (ﷺ), his companions, and the earliest exegetes didn’t discover it, implies that the early Muslims were more ignorant of the message than we are today or that they were too incompetent to discover these things before the non-believers (astaghfir’Allah). Apparently, every learned Muslim prior our century wasn’t capable of interpreting the Qur’an in a way that would allow us to scientifically surpass those who never read the Qur’an to begin with. How profoundly insulting.

Even if you assert that “the Qur’an offers multiple meanings to different people over time”, you’re implying that Allah withheld this information and then only revealed it during a time when non-Muslims have surpassed Muslims in scientific knowledge and technology – thereby making said revelations useless outside a facile appeal to “inspiration” and lacking any moral or intellectual benefit. In other words, to you, the Qur’an’s validity as a Revelation from Allah has been reduced to being measured by contemporary science. How pitiful and unbefitting of a Divine message. Not only that, but you’ve essentially opened the door for the Qur’an to be wrong in the future once the science of the day is replaced by more nuanced theories (as will most likely occur).

I understand what I’m saying is harsh but consider this tough love: if your trust in the Qur’an rests on science, then the problem isn’t the Qur’an, it’s your understanding of Islam.

notes:
THE SPINE. His argument is not 'Islam is pro-science and science proves the Qur'an'. It is a three-part reconstruction. (1) Scientism is a distinct, modern, European doctrine - that the methods and categories of natural science are the only proper elements of any inquiry - and it is in fact 'decidedly unscientific' in Hayek's own sense; he credits Hayek with crystallising the term and quotes Hayek explicitly disavowing any attack on science properly so used. Scientism has three parts in his account: realism, positivism and progressionism. Science as he actually defends it, following Kuhn and the pragmatists (Quine, Popper), is anti-realist, non-progressive and instrumental - theories are models that make the data coherent and are judged on usefulness and coherence, not on truth. (2) The 'classical narrative' (the phrase was coined by its critics, not by orientalists) holds that Muslim science was foreign import plus a conservative religious reaction, with al-Ghazali's Tahafut al-Falasifa as the culprit. He rejects it: scientific productivity kept rising for centuries after al-Ghazali (Ibn al-Nafis on the circulation of the blood, al-Farisi on the rainbow, the critique of Ptolemy); Muslims had flourished precisely because they modified and rejected Aristotle rather than slavishly following him; and the classical narrative is the European Church-and-Galileo story read backwards onto Islamic history. (3) He relabels the 16th-century turn as the 'Age of Dependency' rather than decline, because science was still valued but sourced externally. The cause he advances is precisely the one orientalists deny: a drift into positivism, in which science became 'the measure of all things' and then a standard for reading revelation, so that the Qur'an itself became hostage to whatever science currently said. Revival, in his telling, means stopping borrowing from the dominant civilisation and re-anchoring to one's own values. This is why he attacks the popular 'scientific miracles' defence: it is not a friendly proof of the Qur'an but an instance of the disease he is diagnosing.

SEED TITLES THAT ARE THIN OR ABSENT - do not pad these. 'From Science to Scientism' (_papers/from-science-to-scientism.md) is a link-out stub with no text; the archive's own front matter says the exact slug was lost and points to the successor paper, The Structure of Scientific Productivity in Islamic Civilization. 'The Qur'an and Science: A Forced Marriage' exists twice: the _papers page is a link-out stub, and the _articles page is a Wayback stub whose only real content is the 67-minute MSA OSU halaqa transcript. 'A Muslim's Guide to Science: Scientism' as a written work is a ~390-word Wayback stub; its substance is the five-part Al-Balagh Academy lecture series, of which only Part 1 is embedded on an article page - Parts 2-5 exist as separate transcript pages and are included here individually. 'The Structure of Scientific Productivity...' as a written work is a ~250-word post carrying only the abstract; the full paper is link-out only. 'Islam, Science and History' as a written work is a ~410-word post that is only an embed notice for the interview - but the interview itself is fully preserved on that same article page and is the single richest source in this cluster, so it is cited from there. 'The Rise and Decline of Scientific Productivity in the Muslim World' is the one case where substantive prose survives: the 2015 blog post reproduces the paper's abstract and pages 239-242 with footnotes. Its _papers page states that the 18pp PDF is 'held in this repository', but no PDF file is present in the working tree, so nothing here is quoted from the PDF itself.

NO SUBSTANTIVE TEXT: 'International Conference on Developing Synergies Between Islam and Science and Technology' is a 4-page conference notice co-authored with Daud Batchelor; _papers/international-conference-on-developing-synergies-between-islam-and-science-and-technology.md is a link-out stub with no abstract and no text. 'Islamic Intuitionism: The Case Against Atheistic Evidentialism' (his MA thesis) is also link-out only, and the archive has deliberately WITHHELD the held copy because it reproduces personal identifiers. Neither should be cited as answering any query.

CAVEATS A MAINTAINER MUST CARRY. (a) Almost everything substantive in this cluster is a Whisper machine transcript; the archive's own disclaimer forbids using these in polemics as authoritative. Several quotes contain obvious transcription damage (for example 'Wissenstein' for Wittgenstein, 'totemic' for the geocentric system, 'coron' for Qur'an, 'scientism' for scientism in the Hayek citation, and a stray placeholder token in one French quote). The quotes here are reproduced verbatim including that damage - they prove that the archive holds the passage, not that the wording is his. Prefer the 2015 blog post and the Backbone Ribs paper wherever the same point exists in edited prose, and treat the transcripts as pointers to a video a reader can check rather than as citable text. (b) adam-is-no-myth is a REPUBLICATION of Dr David Jalajel's rebuttal, with only a short framing note by this author; the body is not his argument and must never be presented as his. (c) The French presentation (transcript-DA9JGrHKHZA) is a third party's walkthrough of his paper, in French, machine-transcribed and badly garbled; it is quoted only for the productivity/dependency terminology and the pragmatic-translation point, and should be weighted accordingly. (d) One long_tail query is left in French on purpose (pourquoi lesCBB traduire des textes scientifiques) so the French-language audience has a route into that recording; the CBB token is a transcription artefact, not a word. (e) DO NOT use the Q&A passages in Part 5 or the acknowledgements of the Yaqeen podcast as evidence: they contain his own ill-health remarks and his social-media contact details, which this cluster deliberately excludes under the archive's no-contact policy.

OVERLAP WITH SIBLING CLUSTERS. backbone-ribs and the-quran-science-a-forced-marriage are primarily Qur'an-exegesis works; they are here only for their sustained attack on the 'scientific miracles' methodology, which is a claim about scientism, not tafsir. extraordinary-claims and the Understanding Atheism lecture series (session 2 in particular, which re-teaches Hayek, Popper and Ayer on the same lines) belong primarily to the atheism/epistemology cluster. The 'Information Literacy' lecture (vJRfL4Kal20) discusses the golden age and the destruction of libraries but is not about scientism; its 'scientism' grep hits are false positives for 'information scientist'.

CITATION ROUTES. The two ICR/Yaqeen papers are the scholarly record and are the obvious link-out targets for anyone who wants the argued version; George Saliba's Islamic Science and the Making of the European Renaissance is the historical source he leans on throughout and is named repeatedly here as the readers' next step. Thomas Kuhn's The Structure of Scientific Revolutions is recommended by name in the Al-Balagh course as the required reading.
